video_title: Boogie - Brunson Too Worried About Finals MVP!?!

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins criticizes Jalen Brunson for playing selfishly in Game 3
quotes.excerpt: Brunson was more so worried about the headline, worried about being maybe the Finals MVP.
quotes.quote: The first two games, I would say is whatever. Last night, I didn't like it. I feel like they switched up their style of play as far as allowing the offense to flow through KAT. It seemed like Brunson was more so worried about the headline, worried about being maybe the Finals MVP. That's what I saw in the moment. It didn't seem like it was the right form of basketball last night and I felt it was a lot of forced offense.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons questions why the Knicks moved away from Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: They went away from what they had so much success for in Game 1 and 2.
quotes.quote: The team that's up 2-0 usually doesn't have to make the adjustment. They went away from what they had so much success for in Game 1 and 2. That is playing through Karl-Anthony Towns. That is still playing through him in the elbow, two-man game, high splits, letting him get the ball on the perimeter and attack Victor Wembanyama. Now they made an adjustment, they took Wembanyama off Karl-Anthony Towns, which I thought was smart, letting him play free safety out there and roam. But then again, Karl-Anthony Towns still has a bag. Then he has Jalen Brunson on him, then he has a smaller Castle on him. Then they should really expose that mismatch and even play through Karl-Anthony Towns more, which is why they were up 2-0 on the original first two games.

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins explains why Karl-Anthony Towns struggles to get shot attempts
quotes.excerpt: When it comes to being a big, you obviously receive the ball more than you're dishing it out.
quotes.quote:
Michelle Beadle: I don't get how Karl-Anthony Towns doesn't have a shot until there's less than four minutes left in the first quarter. How do we get here?

DeMarcus Cousins: He's a big. When it comes to being a big, you obviously receive the ball more than you're dishing it out. He's more of a player that needs to depend on the guys around him to get the ball. When you see here and you look at a guy only taking 10 shot attempts or not getting his first attempt until the first quarter is almost over, you have to look at the guys around him. I think it's their job to help him receive the ball.

quotes.speaker: Lou Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Lou Williams credits Spurs' defensive game plan for limiting Karl-Anthony Towns
quotes.excerpt: They put in a pretty good game plan and a scout for Karl-Anthony Towns.
quotes.quote: I'm going to give your team some credit. I think they put in a pretty good game plan and a scout for Karl-Anthony Towns to take away some of the things that's made the game easy for him. Those transition threes that we usually see him, his pick-up points were a little higher last night, so he didn't get those opportunities. Even when he's catching the ball at the top of the key and he likes to put it on the ground, he saw boxes and elbows. That's why you saw Josh Hart getting so many open threes because they said, 'We're willing to die by allowing somebody else to shoot the ball, so we're going to show Karl-Anthony Towns a crowd.'

quotes.speaker: DeMarcus Cousins
quotes.summary_phrase: DeMarcus Cousins and Chandler Parsons debate if the Knicks can get KAT the ball
quotes.excerpt: There's no way in the world you can convince me that Keldon Johnson fronting Karl-Anthony Towns prevents you.
quotes.quote:
DeMarcus Cousins: It's no way in the world you can convince me that Keldon Johnson fronting Karl-Anthony Towns prevents you from finding a way to get him the ball. I won't be convinced.

Chandler Parsons: Keldon Johnson is on you. Aren't you calling for the ball though? You're like, 'Hey, let's stop. We're going over the top. We're going to the rim.'

DeMarcus Cousins: It's no way you can convince me that Keldon Johnson fronting Karl-Anthony Towns prevents you from finding a way to get him the ball. I won't be convinced.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons and DeMarcus Cousins discuss Victor Wembanyama's shove on Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: If somebody did that to Victor Wembanyama, you would be so mad.
quotes.quote:
Chandler Parsons: If somebody did that to Victor Wembanyama, you would be so mad. He barely saw him, he's so little. What do you want him to do?

DeMarcus Cousins: This was dirty as hell. I don't care that there was no whistle on the play. If somebody did that to Victor Wembanyama, you would be so mad. Shaquille O'Neal would be arrested if he did this. I do agree with that. If I did that, they would have probably ejected me, but I'm not mad at him. I'm like, 'Hey, get out the way.'

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons warns Wembanyama about the risks of playing overly physical
quotes.excerpt: He's got to be careful though because this type of stuff will get you tossed from a game.
quotes.quote:
Chandler Parsons: He's got to be careful though because this type of stuff will get you tossed from a game and then your team has zero chance. I like the physicality. This is the same guy that also elbowed Naz Reid directly in the face. I don't think he's targeting little guys.

DeMarcus Cousins: Who's tossing him from a game? The NBA? If he did this to OG or KAT, do we feel a little different? Is it because it's Brunson? It's a short guy. If he does this to the OG or KAT, do we feel a little different?
